title: Release 0.3.0 for the library wave
description: Breaking for 0.x semver: SpaceAddRoleInput.color changed Option<&str> -> Option<serde_json::Value> (with_color now takes impl Into<Value>); MessageQueryInput after/before deprecated and now rejected with InvalidArgument. Also fix doc drift (chat-client PLAN.md:156/158 Blob/copy and Core/echo — echo now exists; README *_query_changes signatures; README RequestError frame — now typed in base-client). Bump all crates to 0.3.0 per RELEASING.md once the library wave is committed.
notes:
Behaviour change (584910de): Space/join now returns forbidden when an active SpaceBan exists for the caller in the target Space; no public API change.
JMAP-yt1w.9 (5542091d): Message/set edits of body/bodyType/mentions/broadcastMentions now return forbidden SetError when senderId != self or deletedAt set; previously applied. No API change.
JMAP-yt1w.2: jmap-chat-types SpaceRole.color changed Option<String> -> Option<serde_json::Value> (spec Color Representation: string, Design Tokens object or CAM16 array). Message gains typed topic_id/subject (Option<String>) and expires_after_read_seconds (Option<u64>); these keys no longer land in Message.extra.
JMAP-yt1w.2: jmap-chat-types RolePatch.color changed Option<Clearable<String>> -> Option<Clearable<serde_json::Value>> so updateRoles accepts all three Color Representation forms.
jmap-chat-types (b82ab4f4): SpaceRole.color Option<String> -> Option<serde_json::Value>; RolePatch.color Option<Clearable<String>> -> Option<Clearable<serde_json::Value>>; Message gains typed topic_id/subject/expires_after_read_seconds (no longer in extra).
JMAP-yt1w.4(i)+(g): jmap-chat-types Chat and Space gain pub closed_at: Option<UTCDate> (wire closedAt); both structs are #[non_exhaustive] so this is semver-minor, but a closedAt on the wire now lands in the typed field instead of extra. jmap-chat-server Chat/set update now rejects closedAt and activeCallId with invalidProperties; previously they were merged into the stored Chat (activeCallId via extra).
yt1w.4(i)+(g) 9e2e052c: chat-types Chat/Space gain pub closed_at: Option<UTCDate> (closedAt, omitted when None; #[non_exhaustive] so semver-minor; wire closedAt now lands in typed field, not extra). chat-server Chat/set updates containing closedAt or activeCallId (incl. null) now rejected with invalidProperties (previously merged into stored Chat).
b14e0c0e: ReadPosition/set create and destroy now return SetError forbidden (draft 1e33ec7 line 1350); Message/set create also creates owner's ReadPosition for the Chat if none.
1535170a (JMAP-yt1w.1(4)): Message/set create now returns invalidArguments for non-empty mentions/broadcastMentions/attachments/actions/replyTo/threadRootId/topicId/subject with application/mls-ciphertext, and for mentions with application/jmap-chat-rich; replyTo/threadRootId on ciphertext were previously accepted (draft line 1727). No public API change.
9f8522cc wire changes: Chat/set kind channel -> forbidden (even with spaceId; channels only via Space/set addChannels); Message/set body >100_000 bytes -> invalidArguments (was invalidProperties [body]); Message/query non-null text/threadRootId -> unsupportedFilter (was silently ignored). No Rust API changes.
a4bc54f9: on the wire, Space/join with a nonexistent or isPublic:false spaceId now returns method error notPermitted instead of forbidden; public Rust API unchanged.
6c1a857a: Space/set last-admin refusal changed forbidden -> invalidProperties ["removeMembers"]; self-removal now allowed without manage_members; apply_space_patch contract table updated; no Rust API signature changes.
JMAP-yt1w.7 (fdc56b3b): ChatLimits gains additive field max_group_chat_members (default 1000) + with_max_group_chat_members; behaviour change: Chat/set update applies addMembers/removeMembers/updateMemberRoles to members and no longer stores them in Chat.extra.
yt1w.4(b) d2f66aa4 wire changes: last-admin leave with members remaining sets closedAt; closed group forbids Message/set create, membership/shared Chat/set updates and self-leave; Message/set create always loads Chat (backend get error -> serverFail).
c294b6d0 (yt1w.4c): closed Spaces refuse Space/set (except self-removal), Space/join, SpaceInvite create, Message create with forbidden; preview includes closedAt; ChatBackend::apply_space_patch MUST set closedAt when last manage_space holder self-removes (third-party backends too).
Breaking (a4602987): Chat/typing now returns invalidArguments 'chatId is not a Chat the account participates in' for unknown chat or non-member group chat (was success); backend lookup error now serverFail (was swallowed). No Rust API changes.
yt1w.4(e) e428e6e9: Message/set broadcastMentions validation failures (out-of-bounds, overflow, missing/non-string scope) now return invalidProperties [broadcastMentions] instead of invalidArguments on the wire; no public API change.
4e476132 behaviour change: client message_update returns InvalidArgument (no network call) for read_disposition without read_at; server Message/set rejects non-null readDisposition without non-null readAt with invalidProperties [readDisposition]. No API changes.
yt1w.5 (68b52eed): Message/set readAt:null now clears readDisposition (previously stored "displayed").
Wire change (JMAP-yt1w.6, cf81ea76): addCategories/updateCategories now move a channel out of its previous category's channelIds instead of listing it in two.
JMAP-yt1w.8 (b0b4d718): no public API change; Space-channel Message/set now calls may_broadcast_mention on create with rich-body broadcast span and on edits whose post-patch message retains a broadcast mention.
JMAP-yt1w.12 (abf6969a): Message/set create/update reject bodyType outside SUPPORTED_BODY_TYPES or non-string (update also rejects null) with invalidProperties [bodyType]; new pub const jmap_chat_server::message::SUPPORTED_BODY_TYPES; testjig supportedBodyTypes adds application/mls-ciphertext.
c9cb992 (JMAP-yt1w.13): No public Rust API changes; jmap-chat-types SpacePatchOp::AddRole(SpaceRole) unchanged, keeps documented placeholder-id contract. Wire: Space/set update addRoles entries without id are now accepted per draft §Space/set ('Server assigns ULIDs'); previously rejected with notUpdated invalidProperties ["addRoles"] (missing field id), which broke every jmap-chat-client SpaceAddRoleInput call. A client-supplied id of any JSON type is now ignored and replaced (before, it had to be a string and was overwritten). MemoryBackend role ids: old = every added role got the same id (default features: role0000000000000001 in every Space); new default = role{n:016x} from a monotonic per-backend counter, unique across all Spaces/accounts in the backend, never reissued after removeRoles. realistic-demo-ids feature unchanged (demo_next_id).
3f21654b (JMAP-yt1w.14): Wire behaviour (jmap-chat-server, Space/set update addCategories): old -> entries without id were rejected with invalidProperties "addCategories[N]: failed to parse entry: missing field id"; new -> entries without id are accepted and the server assigns the category id. A client-supplied id was already overwritten by the backend before this change, and still is (now replaced at parse time with an empty placeholder). Not breaking for conforming clients. No public Rust API change.
b91f9544 (JMAP-yt1w.15): jmap-chat-server MemoryBackend, wire behaviour of Space/set addCategories in the default deterministic id mode (feature realistic-demo-ids off). Old: every category got the id "category0000000000000001", because demo_next_id counts the per-type object map and categories live inside the Space object. New: ids come from a monotonic per-backend counter ("category0000000000000001", "category0000000000000002", ...), unique across Spaces and accounts and never reissued after removeCategories. No public API change (the new field is on the private Inner struct). realistic-demo-ids mode is unchanged.
e2ed330f (JMAP-yt1w.16): Wire behaviour (jmap-chat-server, Message/set create): a valid non-empty `broadcastMentions` array is now stored on the created Message and returned by the create response and Message/get. Before, it was validated and permission-checked, then silently dropped, so the stored array was always []. A `broadcastMentions` value that passes validate_broadcast_mentions but does not deserialize as BroadcastMention[] (for example an entry missing `offset`) is now rejected with invalidProperties ["broadcastMentions"]; before, it was dropped. No public Rust API changes.
2f9f7fbb (JMAP-yt1w.17): jmap-chat-types (public API): Mention { id, offset: u64, length: u64, extra } -> Mention { id, extra }. BroadcastMention { scope, offset: u64, length: u64, extra } -> BroadcastMention { scope, extra }. The offset/length fields are gone (both structs are #[non_exhaustive], so code that reads them breaks). On the wire, offset/length are no longer typed: if a peer sends them, they deserialize into `extra` and round-trip as extension fields.
jmap-chat-server (wire behaviour), Message/set create/update:
(1) rich bodyType with non-empty broadcastMentions: was invalidArguments -> now accepted, stored, and gated by mention_broadcast in channels (forbidden when denied).
(2) rich bodyType with non-empty mentions: was invalidArguments -> now accepted and stored.
(3) rich body "broadcast" span with no broadcastMentions entry: was gated (forbidden without mention_broadcast) on create and edit -> now never gated; spans are not parsed.
(4) mentions/broadcastMentions offset+length bounds or overflow: was invalidProperties -> no longer checked.
ChatBackend::may_broadcast_mention is now called only when post-patch broadcastMentions is non-empty (it was also called for rich broadcast spans).
BREAKING (JMAP-yt1w.21): JmapBackend::query_objects now returns Result<QueryResult, BackendQueryError<Self::Error>> (was Result<QueryResult, Self::Error>). New pub enum jmap_server::BackendQueryError<E> { Method(JmapError), Other(E) } (re-exported from every *-server crate), From<E> so ? on Self::Error still works, From<BackendQueryError<E>> for JmapError (Method passes through, Other -> redacted serverFail). jmap-filenode-server FileNodeBackend::query_subtree now returns Result<Vec<Id>, BackendQueryError<Self::Error>>. jmap-calendars-server QueryCalendarEventsError gains variant Method(JmapError) (non_exhaustive, additive). Wire: /query (generic handle_query and the mail/chat/filenode/calendars /query handlers) now returns a backend's RFC 8620 §5.5 method error (unsupportedFilter, unsupportedSort, anchorNotFound, ...) unchanged instead of serverFail.
77725c9db1657f9d97ae36b201712e5d4c4051ba (JMAP-yt1w.21): Public API (old -> new): 1. jmap-server: JmapBackend::query_objects return type changed from `impl Future<Output = Result<QueryResult, Self::Error>>` to `impl Future<Output = Result<QueryResult, BackendQueryError<Self::Error>>>`. Every JmapBackend implementor must change its signature. Bodies that use `?` on Self::Error keep compiling through `From<E> for BackendQueryError<E>`; a bare `Err(e)` must become `Err(BackendQueryError::Other(e))` or `Err(e.into())`. 2. jmap-server: new `pub enum BackendQueryError<E> { Method(JmapError), Other(E) }`. It is deliberately not #[non_exhaustive] (the split is closed), so downstream crates can convert it exhaustively. It implements Display, std::error::Error (source = Other's inner error), From<E>, and `From<BackendQueryError<E>> for JmapError` (Method is passed through unchanged; Other becomes serverFail with SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC). It is re-exported from jmap-server and from jmap-{mail,chat,calendars,contacts,filenode,sharing,tasks}-server. 3. jmap-filenode-server: FileNodeBackend::query_subtree return type changed from `Result<Vec<Id>, Self::Error>` to `Result<Vec<Id>, BackendQueryError<Self::Error>>`. Its default implementation propagates query_objects errors, and Self::Error cannot hold a method error. Overrides must change their signature. 4. jmap-calendars-server: QueryCalendarEventsError<E> gains a variant `Method(JmapError)`. The enum is already #[non_exhaustive], so this is additive. Wire behaviour (old -> new): when a backend returns BackendQueryError::Method, the client now receives that method error unchanged (type and description). Before, it received serverFail "internal error". This covers RFC 8620 §5.5 errors such as unsupportedFilter, unsupportedSort and anchorNotFound. It applies to generic handle_query (every */query that uses it, including FileNode/query) and to the custom /query handlers: Email, Mailbox and EmailSubmission/query; chat Message, Space, ChatContact and CustomEmoji/query; FileNode/query with depth > 0 (query_subtree); and CalendarEvent/query. Internal backend errors still produce the redacted serverFail. Non-/query callers (the Email lookup during Mailbox/set destroy, and the contacts and calendars cascades) are unchanged. The bundled MemoryBackends never return Method, so their behaviour is unchanged. One exception: the mail MemoryBackend's query_changes maps a Method error from its own query_objects call to cannotCalculateChanges, but that backend's query_objects never returns Method today.
JMAP-yt1w.22 breaking: JmapBackend::query_objects(caller, account_id, filter, sort, limit, position) -> query_objects(caller, account_id, filter, sort, limit, position, anchor: Option<&Id>, anchor_offset: i64); implementors MUST apply RFC 8620 §5.5 anchor rules (jmap_server::resolve_query_start does it for an in-memory id list). Wire: */query via handle_query and chat Message/Space/ChatContact/CustomEmoji/query now honour anchor/anchorOffset (previously silently ignored -> position page), return anchorNotFound for an absent anchor, and invalidArguments for a non-string anchor or non-integer anchorOffset. jmap-filenode-server MemoryBackend now honours position and reports total before limit. New pub fns: jmap_server::query_anchor_args, jmap_server::resolve_query_start.
d8a60f02 (JMAP-yt1w.22): Public API (jmap-server): JmapBackend::query_objects changed from (caller, account_id, filter, sort, limit: Option<u64>, position: i64) to (caller, account_id, filter, sort, limit: Option<u64>, position: i64, anchor: Option<&Id>, anchor_offset: i64). This breaks every JmapBackend/ChatBackend implementor. Implementors MUST follow RFC 8620 §5.5: when an anchor is given, ignore position and start at index(anchor) + anchor_offset, clamped to 0; when the anchor is not in the results, return BackendQueryError::Method(JmapError::anchor_not_found()); when no anchor is given, ignore anchor_offset; report the actual start index in QueryResult::position. New pub fns, both additive: jmap_server::query_anchor_args(&Map<String, Value>) -> Result<(Option<Id>, i64), JmapError>; jmap_server::resolve_query_start(ids: &[Id], position: i64, anchor: Option<&Id>, anchor_offset: i64) -> Result<usize, JmapError>. Wire behaviour: these methods used to ignore anchor/anchorOffset and return the position page; they now honour them: every */query that goes through jmap_server::handle_query (Chat/query and the generic queries in the chat, contacts, tasks, sharing, filenode and calendars servers), and the chat-server Message/query, Space/query, ChatContact/query and CustomEmoji/query. They now return anchorNotFound when the anchor is not in the results. They now return invalidArguments when anchor is not a string or null, or anchorOffset is not an integer or null; previously both were silently accepted. jmap-filenode-server MemoryBackend: it used to ignore position, always report position 0, and report total after applying limit; it now honours position and anchor, and total counts all matching results before the limit. Mail-server Email, Mailbox, EmailSubmission and Sieve queries already handled anchor in their own handlers; their behaviour is unchanged.
792f4f35 (JMAP-405z.1): jmap-chat-types: ChatContact has new required public field identity: String (ChatContact JSON without "identity" now fails to deserialize; struct literals must set it). ChatContact::new(id, login, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, blocked) -> ChatContact::new(id, identity: impl Into<String>, login, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, blocked) (new param second). New variant ChatContactProperty::Identity (enum is #[non_exhaustive], not source-breaking). Docs only: ChatContact.id and Mention.id are server-assigned local RFC 8620 Ids; URI/DID forms belong in ChatContact.identity. jmap-chat-server wire: ChatContact/set update patch containing identity, previously accepted with identity silently dropped, is now rejected for that id with notUpdated {"type":"invalidProperties","properties":["identity"]} and nothing in the patch applied.
2fea4cc5 (JMAP-405z.3): Wire behaviour (jmap-chat-server):
- ChatContact/set create: old -> every create returned notCreated {type: "forbidden"}. New -> a create of {identity} succeeds. The server assigns id and sets login = identity, firstSeenAt = lastSeenAt = now, blocked = false.
- Create rejections: a missing identity, a non-string identity, an all-whitespace identity, or any other property gives invalidProperties naming every offending property. An identity that already exists gives alreadyExists with existingId (enforced by the backend). An identity equal to ChatBackend::owner_user_id gives invalidProperties ["identity"].
- MemoryBackend ChatContact/query: old -> the identity filter was ignored. New -> octet-exact identity match.

Public API (additive, but release-note it):
- jmap-chat-server: new provided trait method ChatBackend::owner_user_id(&self, caller, account_id) -> Future<Result<Option<String>, Self::Error>>. It defaults to Ok(None), which skips the owner check. Backends that serve ownerUserId MUST override it. This is not a compile break for implementors.
- jmap-chat-server: ChatBackend::create_object gains a documented contract. Backends MUST reject a duplicate ChatContact identity atomically with AlreadyExists.with_existing_id(existing). Third-party backends that don't do this will allow duplicate contacts, because the handler does not pre-check.
- jmap-chat-server: new #[doc(hidden)] MemoryBackend::set_owner_user_id_for_test.
- jmap-chat-client: new SessionClient::chat_contact_create(&self, identity: &str) -> Result<SetResponse, ClientError>.
- jmap-chat-client: new field ChatContactQueryInput.filter_identity: Option<String>. The struct is #[non_exhaustive] + Default, so this is not a break.
JMAP-405z.2 (breaking): jmap-chat-types removes SenderId (Owner/Contact, wire sentinel "self"); Message.sender_id, Reaction.sender_id, ChatTypingEvent.sender_id, ChatMessageEntry.sender_id and the Message::new / ChatMessageEntry::plaintext / ::encrypted sender_id params are now jmap_types::Id. Wire: chat-server writes the accountId (not "self") as senderId of owner-created Messages and owner reactions; edit/deletedForAll/reaction-modify checks require senderId == accountId (a stored "self" is now forbidden); Message/query hasMention matches only a Mention whose id is the accountId (was: any non-empty mentions).
e8ad58d2 (JMAP-405z.2): jmap-chat-types (public API): jmap_chat_types::SenderId (enum Owner/Contact(String), its Serialize/Deserialize/Display impls and the wire sentinel "self") is removed. Message.sender_id, Reaction.sender_id, ChatTypingEvent.sender_id and ChatMessageEntry.sender_id change from SenderId to jmap_types::Id. The sender_id parameter of Message::new, ChatMessageEntry::plaintext and ChatMessageEntry::encrypted changes from SenderId to Id. Migration: replace SenderId::Owner with the accountId, SenderId::Contact(s) with Id::from(s), and owner tests (== SenderId::Owner) with sender_id == account_id. jmap-chat-server (wire behaviour): Message/set create senderId goes from "self" to the request accountId. Reaction add via reactions/{id}: server-overridden senderId goes from "self" to the accountId. Edit / deletedForAll / reaction modify-or-remove: allowed when senderId is the accountId (was "self"); stored "self" values are now treated as another sender and get forbidden; forbidden description strings now say "the accountId" instead of "\"self\"". Message/query hasMention: true matches when some mentions[].id equals the accountId (was: any non-empty mentions); broadcastMentions behaviour unchanged. Data migration note: existing stored data with senderId "self" will no longer be recognised as owner-authored.
ebb6318f (JMAP-yt1w.29): Wire behaviour (jmap-chat-server), for backends whose principal_id(caller) differs from the accountId. No public API signature changes; only private fns changed (apply_member_patch_keys param rename, validate_space_patch_ops gains account_id).
- Chat/set group create: creator ChatMember.id and each initial member's invitedBy: principal -> accountId.
- Chat/set addMembers invitedBy: principal -> accountId.
- Chat/set member patch keys: admin check and self-leave key on the accountId. removeMembers [principal] is no longer self-leave; removeMembers [accountId] is self-leave.
- Chat/typing group participation check: principal -> accountId.
- Space/join: new SpaceMember.id, the already-member check and the SpaceBan check (userId) use the accountId instead of the principal.
- Space/set: self-removal (closed-Space exemption, manage_members and last-admin exemptions) and self-nick are recognised only for the accountId, not the principal. The leaving-last-manage_space close keys on the accountId.
- SpaceBan/set bannedBy, SpaceInvite/set createdBy, CustomEmoji/set createdBy: principal -> accountId.
- Single-user posture (principal_id == None), MemoryBackend: removeMembers [accountId] is now self-removal. It is exempt from last-admin protection, and when the leaver holds manage_space and others remain it sets closedAt. Before, self-removal and the close never fired without a principal.
c806303d (JMAP-405z.5): jmap-chat-server: `ChatLimits` gains two public fields, `supported_body_types: &'static [&'static str]` (default `message::SUPPORTED_BODY_TYPES`) and `server_reserved_body_types: &'static [&'static str]` (default `&[]`), plus const setters `with_supported_body_types` and `with_server_reserved_body_types`. The struct is `#[non_exhaustive]` and stays Copy/Eq, so this is additive for callers that use `ChatLimits::new`/`default`. Wire behaviour: Message/set now checks `bodyType` against `ChatBackend::limits(caller, account).supported_body_types` and no longer uses the fixed `SUPPORTED_BODY_TYPES` const. Defaults are unchanged, so nothing changes for backends that keep the default limits. When a backend configures a list, two things change. (1) Any type in that list is accepted, and any type not in it gets invalidProperties["bodyType"]. If the list leaves out text/plain (E2EE-only), an explicit "text/plain" and an omitted bodyType are now rejected; before, they were accepted. (2) A Message/set create using a type in `server_reserved_body_types` now gets SetError `invalidArguments`; before, it was accepted if listed. Message/set update ignores the reserved list. `SUPPORTED_BODY_TYPES` is still public; it is now documented as the default list.
fb63f6bb (JMAP-yt1w.32): Wire behaviour, only for backends whose JmapBackend::principal_id returns Some(p) with p != accountId (single-user mode, principal_id None, is unchanged):
- Space/get member classification. Old: the caller is a member iff some members[].id == principal_id(caller). New: iff some members[].id == the request accountId. A Space whose members list the principal but not the accountId now returns notFound (non-previewable) or the restricted preview. One that lists the accountId now returns the full view.
- Space/set permission and role-hierarchy gates (structural ops and top-level metadata), SpaceBan/set `ban` gate, and Chat/set pinnedMessageIds gate (group-chat `admin` role and channel `pin` permission). Old: the caller's permissions, highest role position and group role came from the member entry whose id == principal_id(caller). New: they come from the entry whose id == accountId.
Public API (doc-hidden, test-only helpers on memory::MemoryBackend; signatures unchanged): apply_space_patch_with_caller_id, apply_space_metadata_patch_with_caller_id, may_set_pinned_messages_with_caller_id and may_set_space_ban_with_caller_id. Old: caller_id was the member id looked up. New: caller_id only says whether identity is wired (Some vs None), and the lookup uses account_id.
Backend contract (ChatBackend docs on apply_space_metadata_patch, which applies to every caller-membership and permission check in the trait, and may_set_custom_emoji): third-party backends must look up the caller's Space membership and permissions by account_id, the owner's member entry, not by principal_id. Backends that keyed on the principal must switch to the accountId.
JMAP-yt1w.33 breaking changes (jmap-chat-server): (1) MemoryBackend with principal_id None (CallerCtx = ()) now enforces Space/set permission + role-hierarchy gates, manage_space for metadata, pinnedMessageIds gate and SpaceBan ban gate against the owner's member entry (accountId); old: all permitted, new: forbidden when that entry lacks the permission. (2) Removed doc(hidden) MemoryBackend::{apply_space_patch_with_caller_id, apply_space_metadata_patch_with_caller_id, may_set_pinned_messages_with_caller_id, may_set_space_ban_with_caller_id}; use the ChatBackend trait methods. (3) ChatBackend::apply_space_metadata_patch contract no longer lets backends skip the gate when principal_id returns None.
90a18713 (JMAP-yt1w.34): jmap-chat-server wire behaviour: Space/set create previously returned a Space with roles [], members [], memberCount 0. It now returns roles [{"id":"admin","name":"Admin","permissions":[every spec permission],"position":9007199254740991}], members [{"id":<accountId>,"roleIds":["admin"],"joinedAt":<create time>}], memberCount 1. This applies to every ChatBackend because it happens in handle_space_set. Consequence: Space/join by the creator on their own new Space now fails with invalidArguments "caller is already a member of this space"; previously it succeeded. jmap-chat-types: the pub const vocabulary::SPEC_PERMISSION_NAMES gains "start_call" (9 -> 10 entries), matching the draft. Code that relied on its length or contents sees the new entry.
Wire change (JMAP-yt1w.30): /set over maxObjectsInSet now yields method error {type: requestTooLarge, description: maxObjectsInSet} instead of {type: limit, description: maxObjectsInSet}. Affects jmap_server::enforce_max_objects_in_set and every *-server Foo/set handler.
3edb32dd (JMAP-yt1w.30): Wire behaviour: when a Foo/set exceeds maxObjectsInSet, every *-server /set handler now returns a different method error. Old: {type: "limit", description: "maxObjectsInSet"}. New: {type: "requestTooLarge", description: "maxObjectsInSet"}. It still arrives as an "error" invocation in methodResponses at HTTP 200, and later method calls in the same request still run, as before. Public API: jmap_server::enforce_max_objects_in_set (and the crate::helpers re-exports) changes its Err value from JmapError::limit("maxObjectsInSet") to JmapError::request_too_large() with description Some("maxObjectsInSet"). The signature is unchanged. Rust callers matching on error_type == "limit" must switch to "requestTooLarge".
3498a6f4 (JMAP-yt1w.31): Wire behaviour: a /get call whose `ids` array has more than 500 entries (the default cap) now returns the method-level error {"type":"requestTooLarge","description":"maxObjectsInGet"} in place of the Foo/get response. Before this change the call was processed with no cap. This applies to the generic jmap_server::handle_get, so every extension /get that delegates to it changes too (Chat, Calendar, CalendarEventNotification, ParticipantIdentity, AddressBook, ContactCard, Principal, ShareNotification, TaskList, Task, TaskNotification, FileNode). It also applies to the custom handlers: Space, Message, SpaceBan, SpaceInvite, PresenceStatus, ChatContact, ReadPosition, CustomEmoji, VacationResponse, EmailSubmission, Thread, Email, Mailbox, Identity, SieveScript and CalendarEvent. A null or absent `ids` is not counted. Public API, additive only: new provided trait method `JmapBackend::max_objects_in_get(&self, caller, account_id) -> u64` (default 500), and new pub fn `jmap_server::enforce_max_objects_in_get(&Map<String, Value>, u64) -> Result<(), JmapError>`, re-exported at the crate root. There is a semver hazard: a downstream type that already has an inherent or other-trait method named `max_objects_in_get` could hit method-resolution ambiguity. Backends that advertise a Session maxObjectsInGet other than 500 must override the new method to match.
e5eddc27 (JMAP-yt1w.35): Wire behaviour, jmap-chat-server MemoryBackend: Message/set create or update in a channel Chat used to accept any non-empty broadcastMentions (permit-all default). It now returns forbidden ("caller lacks required permission `mention_broadcast` in this Space") unless the owner's member entry (accountId) has mention_broadcast in its effective Space permissions. Group and direct chats outside a Space are unchanged (the handler skips the gate), and a Space that no longer exists is still permitted. Public API, additive only: new `jmap_chat_server::permissions::MENTION_BROADCAST: &str = "mention_broadcast"`. The ChatBackend trait default for may_broadcast_mention is unchanged (still permit-all).
b8b6f251 (JMAP-yt1w.36): jmap-chat-server wire behaviour, Space/get. Old: when JmapBackend::principal_id returned None (single-user mode, e.g. MemoryBackend with CallerCtx = ()), the caller was treated as a member of every Space and always got the full Space object. New: membership always keys on the members entry whose id is the request accountId (the owner, per draft §Terminology), whatever principal_id returns. A Space with no accountId member entry is reported in notFound when isPubliclyPreviewable is false, and returned as the restricted view (id, name, description, iconBlobId, memberCount, createdAt, isPublic, isPubliclyPreviewable, closedAt) when it is true. No public Rust API change: the only signatures that changed are on the private helpers non_member_non_previewable and project_space_for_caller (Option<&Id> -> &Id).
2641a8fc (JMAP-yt1w.38): Wire behaviour of jmap-mail-server SearchSnippet/get. Old: any number of emailIds was accepted and passed to the backend. New: when emailIds has more entries than JmapBackend::max_objects_in_get(caller, accountId) (default 500), the call fails with the method-level error {"type":"requestTooLarge","description":"maxObjectsInGet"} and the backend is not called (RFC 8621 Section 5.1). Exactly the cap is still processed. The public Rust API is unchanged: no signatures changed and no new config knob was added.
270da180 (JMAP-nbk3.1): jmap-types (additions): new module jmap_types::push and root re-exports of StateChange, PushSubscription, PushKeys and PushVerification. All four are #[non_exhaustive] and have an extra map. PushSubscription and PushKeys derive serde. Every PushSubscription property except deviceClientId is an Option, omitted on serialize when None. PushKeys requires both p256dh and auth on deserialize. PushSubscription.id and PushVerification.push_subscription_id are typed Id. jmap-base-client StateChange: it now re-exports jmap_types::StateChange, and both jmap_base_client::StateChange and jmap_base_client::push::StateChange still resolve. The wire behaviour changes, old -> new: (1) Serialize: emitted no @type -> always emits "@type":"StateChange". (2) Deserialize via serde: "@type" was captured into extra -> it is consumed and never appears in extra. A missing @type is still accepted. Any other @type value -> error (previously accepted into extra). (3) SSE: an event: state payload whose @type is present but not "StateChange" was parsed as SseEvent::StateChange -> now SseEvent::Unknown. (4) WebSocket frames: no behaviour change, because dispatch already required @type == "StateChange". (5) StateChange no longer has derived Serialize/Deserialize impls (they are hand-written); a downstream crate that relied on serde attributes or field ordering would notice. Debug output: PushSubscription, PushKeys and PushVerification have hand-written Debug impls that print [REDACTED] for url, keys.auth and verificationCode. This is new API, so nothing existing breaks.
438c3bde (JMAP-nbk3.3): jmap-server PushSubscriptionBackend gains three required methods: create_push_subscription(&self, caller, new: PushSubscription) -> Result<StoredPushSubscription, BackendSetError<Self::Error>>; update_push_subscription(&self, caller, sub: PushSubscription) -> Result<PushSubscription, BackendSetError<Self::Error>>; destroy_push_subscription(&self, caller, id: &Id) -> Result<(), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>. Old: only list_push_subscriptions; new: four methods. Wire: register_push_subscription_handlers now also registers PushSubscription/set (was unknownMethod): standard /set without accountId/oldState/newState, ignores accountId/ifInState; invalidProperties for non-https url, create with id or verificationCode, change to id/deviceClientId/url/keys (unchanged allowed), wrong verificationCode; expires clamped/defaulted to now + 7 days and echoed; created carries id, expires and every stored property the client omitted (null when unset, incl. verificationCode, types; backend extension props too); updated holds {expires} when it differs from request else null; non-empty update lists stored subscriptions before any create, list failure is method-level serverFail with nothing committed. Additions: jmap-server MAX_PUSH_EXPIRY_SECS, is_deliverable, state_change_for, utc_date_from_epoch_seconds, runtime dep subtle (workspace 2.6); jmap-types StateChange::new(changed) (StateChange is non_exhaustive).
1040195 (JMAP-nbk3.5): jmap-chat-server, public API: additions only. New pub mod push with validate_chat_push(&Map, &HashMap<Id, ChatPushCapability>) -> Result<(), SetError>, strip_unsupported_chat_push(&mut Map, &HashMap<Id, ChatPushCapability>) and chat_state_change_for(&PushSubscription, &HashMap<Id, HashMap<String, State>>, &HashMap<Id, ChatPushCapability>) -> Option<StateChange>, all re-exported at crate root. memory::MemoryBackend::set_chat_push_capability_for_test(&Id, Option<ChatPushCapability>) is new and doc(hidden). Behaviour change in MemoryBackend PushSubscriptionBackend (memory feature only): create/update with a non-null chatPush entry now rejected with invalidProperties (chatPush, chatPush/<acct>, or chatPush/<acct>/{kinds,properties,urgency,mentionUrgency}) unless the account has a capability set via the new setter (none by default, so any non-null entry is rejected). list_push_subscriptions now drops chatPush entries for accounts without the capability; an empty {} map is left in place. No wire change for handler consumers: chat-server register functions still do not wire PushSubscription handlers.
9ea09267 (JMAP-nbk3.6): jmap-chat-types, ChatMessageEntry: six fields changed type. message_id: Id -> Option<Id>; chat_id: Id -> Option<Id>; chat_kind: ChatKind -> Option<ChatKind>; sender_id: Id -> Option<Id>; sent_at: UTCDate -> Option<UTCDate>; encrypted: bool -> Option<bool>. Each now has #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]. Wire effects: (1) Deserialize now accepts an entry that is missing any of these keys, where it used to fail. (2) Serialize leaves out a key whose value is None. The ChatMessageEntry::plaintext() and ::encrypted() signatures are unchanged and still set all six fields to Some, so their output is byte-identical to before. Additions in jmap-chat-server, re-exported at the crate root: pub fn build_chat_message_push(&Id, State, &ChatPushConfig, &ChatPushCapability, OwnerFlags, PushItem<'_>) -> BuiltPush; pub struct OwnerFlags { active, admin }; pub struct PushItem<'a> { message, chat, sender, sender_member, space }; pub struct BuiltPush { payload, urgency }. PushItem::space is Option<&'a Space>, the Space containing a channel Chat; its name becomes spaceName. These three structs are deliberately not #[non_exhaustive], because the regression tests build them with struct literals. Adding a field to any of them later (for example JMAP-yt1w.42) is therefore a breaking change.
